title: Provenance schema: required verified object (subject_digest/as_of/recorded_at), PROV-O vocabulary
description: ODOC-231 Decision SS5-6. verified becomes a required object, never a bare date: subject_digest (required - the exact bytes measured), as_of (required - when the claim was last known true), recorded_at (required - when the assertion was authored), stale_after (optional - recheck boundary), subject_name (optional, non-authoritative label). Absent stale_after means UNKNOWN, never FRESH. A re-verification is a NEW record pointing at the old digest, never an edit to the old verified: field in place (OCI referrers pattern) - editing in place destroys verification history. Add PROV-O vocabulary (derived_from, revision_of, specialization_of, generated_at, invalidated_at) as short frontmatter names inside the EXISTING relations axis - do not open a second relation axis - each bound to its PROV IRI in one machine-readable schema table. Each document names the schema it was authored against and that name is never rewritten; use FULL_TRANSITIVE compatibility (this corpus is a permanent archive); never add a required field going forward, only optional-with-default, enforcing required-ness as a lint on new documents rather than a schema constraint, so history is never invalidated. Guard per Decision SS6: version identity (the new content-addressed blob SHA from LCLI-547) is a fourth independent axis alongside lifecycle status/delivery rollup/claim state (ADR-0019/0021) and must NOT be derived from or feed claim_version - a hash changing on a typo fix must not flag every dependent for review.

acceptanceCriteria.text: verified is a required object with required subject_digest, as_of, recorded_at; stale_after and subject_name are optional; absent stale_after is read as UNKNOWN not FRESH
A re-verification creates a new record referencing the prior digest rather than editing verified: in place
derived_from/revision_of/specialization_of/generated_at/invalidated_at exist inside the existing relations axis (no second axis), each mapped to its PROV IRI in one schema table
Schema evolution never adds a required field to existing documents; new required-ness is enforced as a lint on newly authored docs only
claim_version remains author-declared and is never derived from the new content-addressed revision identity
